reference_solution.expected_approach: Sort the intervals by their starting values and then merge overlapping intervals while traversing the sorted intervals.
reference_solution.why: Sorting places overlapping or potentially overlapping intervals next to each other, allowing each interval to be compared with the most recently merged interval and reducing the problem to a single traversal after sorting.
detailed_explanation: Sort all intervals by their starting value.
Create an empty result list for the merged intervals.
Add the first interval to the result.
For each remaining interval, compare its start with the end of the last interval in the result.
If the current interval overlaps with the last merged interval, extend the end of the last interval to the maximum of the two end values.
If the intervals do not overlap, add the current interval to the result.
Continue until all intervals have been processed.
pseudocode: Sort the intervals by their starting value.
For each interval in the sorted intervals:
If the result is empty or the current interval does not overlap with the last result interval, add the current interval.
Otherwise, merge the current interval with the last result interval by updating its end to the maximum of both ends.
reasoning_steps: Sort the intervals by their starting values.
Compare each interval with the last merged interval.
Merge the intervals if they overlap.
Add the interval separately if they do not overlap.
Continue until all intervals are processed.
edge_cases: Intervals with the same starting value

alternative_solutions.name: Repeated Overlap Merging
alternative_solutions.description: Repeatedly scan the intervals for overlapping pairs, merge each overlapping pair, and continue until no overlapping intervals remain.
